findings.title: Queued-call cancellation on disconnect is not implementable with the specified interfaces
findings.evidence: Section 2.4: "`CancellationToken` causes the `TaskScheduler` to transition the task to `Canceled` without executing the delegate." Section 6.5: "If `CallId` is new: enqueue and track as `Queued`." Section 9.2: "`Queued` calls → marked `Cancelled`. Their Tasks are completed with `OperationCanceledException`."
findings.problem: The spec requires disconnect handling to cancel already-enqueued tool calls, but it does not define any per-call `CancellationTokenSource`, queue handle, or dequeue API that `DisconnectHandler`/`ToolCallRegistry` can use to cancel posted work before the UI thread starts it.
findings.why_it_matters: Without a concrete cancellation hook, queued commands can still run after the registry says `Cancelled`, causing post-disconnect model mutations and making reconnect behavior nondeterministic.
findings.proposed_fix: Define ownership of a per-call `CancellationTokenSource` in the registry and require that token to be passed into `ISwCommandQueue.ExecuteAsync`, or extend `ISwCommandQueue` with a removable work-item handle and specify exact state-transition ordering during disconnect.

findings.title: Oversized WebSocket message handling leaves the connection state undefined
findings.evidence: "A maximum message size of 1 MB is enforced; messages exceeding this limit are rejected with `AddinProtocolErrorMessage(ErrorCode = "MESSAGE_TOO_LARGE")` and the accumulated buffer is discarded."
findings.problem: Discarding only the accumulated buffer is insufficient for a fragmented WebSocket message. The spec does not say whether the receiver must continue reading and discarding frames until `EndOfMessage`, or close the socket immediately.
findings.why_it_matters: If unread frames from the oversized message remain on the socket, the next `ReceiveAsync` continues the same message and corrupts message framing for all subsequent traffic.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify one required behavior: either drain and discard until `EndOfMessage` before resuming normal reads, or close the WebSocket with a message-too-large policy and reset session state.

findings.title: Handshake ordering depends on client behavior because the server-side gate is unspecified
findings.evidence: Section 6.3 step 5 sends `StateUpdateMessage(Trigger = InitialState)` and step 6 says "Client may now send `IClientMessage`s." Section 6.4 says "Dispatches incoming messages by polymorphic type."
findings.problem: The document states when the client should start sending, but it does not define what the add-in does if messages arrive before the initial state snapshot is sent or before handshake completion is recorded server-side.
findings.why_it_matters: A pipelined `tool_call` can race the initial `StateUpdateMessage`, breaking the stated ordering guarantees around `StateVersion` and allowing model mutation before the baseline snapshot exists.
findings.proposed_fix: Define an explicit handshake state in `MessageDispatcher`: do not dispatch `IClientMessage`s until `AddinReadyMessage` and the initial state snapshot have been sent, or reject/buffer pre-handshake messages with a dedicated protocol error.

findings.title: Screenshot path validation contradicts the stated read-only ownership model
findings.evidence: Section 7.2: "The orchestrator is read-only." Section 7.4: "The orchestrator validates that this path is readable from its process context by creating and deleting a temporary file."
findings.problem: Creating and deleting a file tests write access, not read access, and directly violates the declared rule that the orchestrator is read-only.
findings.why_it_matters: This fails in deployments where the orchestrator legitimately has only read permission to the shared directory, and it widens filesystem permissions beyond what the spec claims is required.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the temp-file probe with a true read/accessibility check, or define an add-in-written probe file that the orchestrator only reads.

findings.title: `AddinSessionId` uniqueness guarantee is stronger than the implementation provides
findings.evidence: Section 8.1: "guaranteed to change on add-in reload" and the implementation uses `var loadTimestamp = DateTime.UtcNow.Ticks;` as part of the input.
findings.problem: `DateTime.UtcNow.Ticks` is not a monotonic unique reload identifier. Rapid reloads in the same process or clock rollback can produce the same input tuple, so the stated guarantee is not actually established by the algorithm.
findings.why_it_matters: If a session ID repeats, stale-epoch detection and `ToolCallRegistry` scoping can collide across add-in reloads.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a random 128-bit value (`Guid.NewGuid()` or equivalent) for `AddinSessionId`, or weaken the document language to probabilistic uniqueness and state the collision assumptions explicitly.

top_3_must_fix: Define a concrete cancellation mechanism for queued tool calls so disconnect-time `Cancelled` behavior can actually be enforced.
Specify mandatory oversized-WebSocket handling that drains the rest of the message or closes the socket to preserve framing.
Add a server-side handshake gate so `IClientMessage`s cannot execute before the initial state snapshot is sent.
